question.text: A trader is long one USDINR futures contract at 84.00 and simultaneously sells one 84.50 call at a premium of Rs. 0.15. At expiry, USDINR = 84.30. What is the total payoff per unit from the combined position?

explanation.text: The Logic: Long-futures payoff = expiry - entry = 84.30 - 84.00 = +0.30 per unit. The short 84.50 call is out of the money at expiry (84.30 is below 84.50), so it expires worthless and the seller keeps the full 0.15 premium. Combined payoff per unit = 0.30 + 0.15 = Rs. 0.45. The Trap: Rs. 0.30 counts only the futures leg. Rs. 0.15 counts only the option premium. Rs. 0.65 would require the call to also pay out, but at expiry 84.30 is below the 84.50 strike so the call is not exercised. Note: Stem reworded as a long-futures-plus-short-call component-payoff question to avoid the unsupported covered-call label; the broken explanation sentence after "Short call: OTM (84.30" has been repaired.
